question: Barium sulphate, used as a contrast agent in GI radiology ('barium meal'), is toxic because barium is a heavy metal poison.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. BaSO₄ is non-toxic because of its extreme insolubility. Only soluble barium salts are toxic — they release Ba²⁺ ions in the stomach (acidic environment dissolves the salt), which then block potassium channels, causing hypokalaemia and potentially fatal muscle paralysis including respiratory failure.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Barium sulphate (BaSO₄) is completely insoluble in body fluids and therefore NON-TOXIC — it passes through the GI tract without absorption. Toxic barium poisoning is caused by SOLUBLE salts (barium carbonate, chloride, nitrate) used in rodenticides.
